title: Saturation / Queue / Throttle Playbook - Data Pull & Analysis
content:
Purpose:
This working doc collects the data pull queries, derived metrics, visualization recipes, and first-draft runbook steps we used during the Jan 2026 GPU fleet capacity incident (ticket JIRA-INC-1243). The goal is to make it easy for on-call and infra analysts to reproduce the postmortem slices that matter for saturation, queueing, and throttling analysis, and to capture short-term mitigations and longer-term automations.

Context / short summary:
- On 2026-02-18 we observed a multi-region latency/regression event tied to sustained GPU saturation in eu-west and us-west (canary signals first). Symptoms: sudden rise in P95 generation latency, increase in throttled requests, and degraded throughput for Dedicated customers with strict SLOs.
- This doc focuses on the data pulls and derived signals we found most useful when diagnosing: per-GPU saturation ratio, per-host queue depth (KV and scheduling), throttle counts by policy, and inverse correlations with autoscaler decisions.

Quick TL;DR findings (working hypotheses):
1) A shift in batch-size distribution (client-side) increased average sequence length and per-request GPU memory working set; on some older nodes this pushed active memory usage above the liveliness threshold causing active eviction and longer scheduling latency.
2) Autoscaler lag combined with regional burst traffic created transient pinning of requests onto a hot subset of instances, amplifying queue depth and causing local throttles to trip.
3) Throttle policy and graceful-fallback paths are currently blind to per-instance eviction/oom-retry rates; adding eviction rate into routing decisions would have shortened outage window.

Data sources referenced:
- BigQuery tables: infra_telemetry.gpu_metrics_v2, infra_telemetry.request_traces_v3, infra_telemetry.autoscaler_events, infra_telemetry.throttle_events, infra_telemetry.kv_cache_evictions
- Redis/KV eviction logs (s3://redwood-logs/evictions/2026-02-18/*)
- Control-plane event stream (kinesis:region-autoscale-events)
- Customer-facing metrics (datadog:dedicated.*)

Derived metrics and SQL slices (copy/paste runnable, adjust time windows):
1) Per-GPU saturation ratio (5-min): fraction of time GPU compute utilization >= 85%
```
SELECT
  timestamp_trunc(ts, MINUTE, 5) as window,
  region,
  instance_id,
  AVG(CASE WHEN gpu_util_percent >= 85 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as saturation_fraction,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(gpu_util_percent, 100)[OFFSET(95)] as p95_util
FROM infra_telemetry.gpu_metrics_v2
WHERE ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(TIMESTAMP('2026-02-18 00:00:00'), INTERVAL 1 HOUR)
              AND TIMESTAMP_ADD(TIMESTAMP('2026-02-18 00:00:00'), INTERVAL 6 HOUR)
GROUP BY window, region, instance_id
ORDER BY window, region;
```
2) Per-host request queue depth and scheduling delay (p90, p99) aggregated by 1-min slice:
```
SELECT
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(req_ts, MINUTE) as minute,
  host_id,
  COUNT(1) as inflight_count,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(sched_delay_ms, 0.90) as p90_sched_ms,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(sched_delay_ms, 0.99) as p99_sched_ms
FROM infra_telemetry.request_traces_v3
WHERE req_ts BETWEEN '2026-02-18 02:00:00' AND '2026-02-18 04:30:00'
  AND route LIKE '%generation%'
GROUP BY minute, host_id
ORDER BY minute;
```
3) Throttle event rollup by policy and region (1-min):
```
SELECT
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(event_ts, MINUTE) as minute,
  region,
  throttle_policy,
  COUNT(1) as throttle_count
FROM infra_telemetry.throttle_events
WHERE event_ts BETWEEN '2026-02-18 01:30:00' AND '2026-02-18 05:00:00'
GROUP BY minute, region, throttle_policy
ORDER BY minute, region;
```
4) Eviction spikes correlated to queue depth (join kv_cache_evictions to request traces):
```
SELECT
  t.minute,
  t.host_id,
  t.p90_sched_ms,
  e.evictions_in_min
FROM (
  SELECT TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(req_ts, MINUTE) as minute, host_id, PERCENTILE_CONT(sched_delay_ms,0.90) as p90_sched_ms
  FROM infra_telemetry.request_traces_v3
  WHERE req_ts BETWEEN '2026-02-18 02:00:00' AND '2026-02-18 04:30:00'
  GROUP BY minute, host_id
) t
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(eviction_ts, MINUTE) as minute, host_id, COUNT(1) as evictions_in_min
  FROM infra_telemetry.kv_cache_evictions
  WHERE eviction_ts BETWEEN '2026-02-18 02:00:00' AND '2026-02-18 04:30:00'
  GROUP BY minute, host_id
) e
ON t.minute = e.minute AND t.host_id = e.host_id
ORDER BY t.minute DESC;
```
Notes on interpretation and pitfalls:
- gpu_util_percent has sampling noise at 1s resolution; prefer 1-5m aggregations for signal stability.
- sched_delay_ms includes both queueing time and OS scheduling jitter; compare p90 against a baseline day to detect anomalies.
- Throttle events may be emitted by multiple subsystems: per-tenant, per-region, and node-level. Always join with throttle_source or policy to disambiguate.

Visualization recipes (for the postmortem slides and the incident dashboard):
- Top-left: regional P95 latency (client-observed) vs regional average GPU util (dual y-axis). Annotate autoscaler events as vertical lines.
- Top-right: heatmap of per-host p99 sched_delay over time (hosts on y, time on x) to spot hotspots.
- Bottom-left: throttle_count stacked by policy, time series.
- Bottom-right: scatterplot minute-by-minute: p90_sched_ms vs evictions_in_min (color by host).

Initial investigative findings (raw):
- eu-west-1: 18:10-18:35 UTC saw sustained saturation_fraction > 0.9 on 24% of instances; p99 scheduling delay spiked to >1200ms on 6 hosts.
- Hosts with highest eviction rates had older CUDA driver patch level (driver-11.7.0) compared with fleet median (11.8.6), and showed higher GC-related stall times in kernel logs.
- Autoscaler scale-out request occurred at 18:15 but allocation-to-ready lag was ~7m due to constrained spare capacity in eu-west AZ-a. The autoscaler then routed new traffic unevenly while the hot hosts were still draining.

Immediate mitigations executed during the incident (ops timeline):
- 18:22 - Emergency temporary routing: increased cross-region fallback from 10% -> 35% for non-strict SLO traffic (runbook: /runbooks/cross-region-fallback).
- 18:29 - Manual gentle drain of 8 worst hosts; moved ~avg 15 ongoing requests each before drain to avoid hard OOM restarts.
- 18:36 - Throttle policy for node-level throttles adjusted to raise threshold by +10% to reduce noisy trips while scale-out completed.

Runbook: checklist for next on-call (short):
1) Pull 1-min per-host p99 scheduling delay and sort top 10 hosts.
2) For top hosts: check eviction rate and driver version (bq + s3 logs).
3) If eviction_rate/min > 2 and p99_sched_ms > 800ms, mark host for gentle drain.
4) Check autoscaler event lag: diff(alloc_request_ts, instance_ready_ts) > 3m => escalate to infra-alloc team.
5) If >30% of region hosts are saturated_fraction > 0.85 for 10 continuous minutes, enable cross-region fallback (pre-approved knob).

Automation proposals (longer-term):
- Add eviction_rate as a routing signal: when eviction_rate/min rises above threshold, temporarily divert 20% of incoming requests away from host for up to 5m. (Owner: Priya Nair, ETA: Q2 2026)
- Cross-layer backpressure: integrate scheduler queue depth (p90) into autoscaler decision window so scale-out is triggered earlier when queueing grows faster than util. (Owner: Miguel Ortega, ETA: Q3 2026)
- Fleet maintenance tagging: mark hosts with older driver kernels, route Canary/burst traffic away until patched. (Owner: SRE team, ETA: Q2 2026)

Follow-ups / action items (triage board snippets):
- INFR-8721: automate the data pull and dashboard (Claire) — due 2026-03-15.
- INFR-8722: implement eviction-rate routing prototype (Priya) — due 2026-06-01.
- INFR-8723: reduce allocation-to-ready tail by improving AZ placement (Miguel) — analysis due 2026-04-01.

Appendix: quick checks to run on-call (one-liners):
- Top host p99 scheduling delay:
  bq query --nouse_legacy_sql \"SELECT host_id, PERCENTILE_CONT(sched_delay_ms,0.99) from infra_telemetry.request_traces_v3 WHERE req_ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 15 MINUTE) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() GROUP BY host_id ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10\"
- Eviction spike finder (last 30m):
  bq query --nouse_legacy_sql \"SELECT host_id, COUNT(1) as evictions FROM infra_telemetry.kv_cache_evictions WHERE eviction_ts > TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 MINUTE) GROUP BY host_id ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 20\"
- Autoscaler lag sample:
  bq query --nouse_legacy_sql \"SELECT cluster, COUNTIF(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(instance_ready_ts, alloc_request_ts, SECOND) > 180) as slow_allocs FROM infra_telemetry.autoscaler_events WHERE alloc_request_ts > TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 6 HOUR) GROUP BY cluster\"

Notes-to-self / unresolved questions:
- Need to reconcile driver patch mapping (fleet metadata) with evictions table; current join is imperfect due to missing host tags. Create small lookup table host_meta.host_driver_version.
- Confirm whether per-tenant throttles (customer-surface) differ from node-level throttle semantics — I've seen ambiguous policy names in throttle_events. Follow up with routing team.

If you're using this doc during an incident: copy the SQL queries into the incident sheet, run them for the incident window, and paste the top 10 host lists into #infra-incident with the tag @infra-oncall.

---
